en: to win the victory; to win the title

examples.en: Our team wins the championship.
A Korean player won the tournament.
I will win the title this year for sure.
Everyone shouted the moment they won.
You have to practice hard to win the title.
He is a player who won three times in a row.

explain: '우승하다'는 대회에서 일등을 할 때 써요. 대회 이름은 '~에서 우승하다'로 말해요. 일상의 '일등 하다'나 '이기다'는 시합 하나를 이길 때도 쓰지만 '우승'은 전체 결과예요.

phrases.en: Our team took the championship.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우승하다'보다 결과를 얻었다는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes having claimed the title.

phrases.en: The player lifted the trophy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우승한 장면을 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to picture the moment of winning.

phrases.en: Our team is a title contender.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우승할 가능성이 큰 팀이나 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a team or person likely to win.

explain_en: 우승하다 is used when you take first place in a tournament. The event takes 에서, as in '~에서 우승하다'. 이기다 can mean winning a single match, but 우승 refers to the overall result.

examples.ko: 월요일 아침마다 피곤한 걸 월요병이라고 해요.
examples.en: Feeling tired every Monday morning is called Monday blues.
The Monday blues start on Sunday night.
Because of the Monday blues, it's hard to get up in the morning.
I listen to music I like to beat the Monday blues.
Warm coffee is the best for the Monday blues.
Not only workers but students also get the Monday blues.

explain: 진짜 병이 아니라 주말이 끝나고 일이나 학교로 돌아가기 싫은 기분을 농담처럼 말하는 거예요. '월요병이 오다', '월요병에 걸리다'처럼 써요. 피곤하고 의욕이 없을 때 가볍게 말해요.

phrases.en: I caught the Monday blues from Sunday night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 월요일이 싫은 기분이 든다는 걸 농담처럼 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A joking way to say you dread Monday.

phrases.en: The weekend is ending, so the Monday blues are coming.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주말 끝에 기분이 가라앉기 시작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when your mood starts to sink at the end of the weekend.

phrases.en: I beat the Monday blues with a cup of coffee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 월요일의 피곤함을 이겨 낸다는 가벼운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light expression for getting through Monday's tiredness.

explain_en: It isn't a real illness but a joking way to describe not wanting to go back to work or school after the weekend. You say '월요병이 오다' or '월요병에 걸리다'. People use it lightly when they feel tired and unmotivated.

en: to be pregnant; to become pregnant; to be in the family way

examples.en: My older sister got pregnant not long ago.
When you're pregnant, you have to be careful about what you eat.
I gave my seat to a pregnant friend.
I'm on leave from work because I'm pregnant.
I got checked at the hospital before getting pregnant.
We are getting ready to have a baby.

explain: 지금 임신 중인 상태는 과거형 '임신했어요'로 말해요. 가까운 사이에서는 '아기가 생겼어요'라고도 해요. 병원이나 뉴스에서는 '임신'을 써요.

phrases.en: My friend is pregnant right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 임신한 상태를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the current state of being pregnant.

phrases.en: I heard that my neighbor is pregnant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람에게 들은 소식을 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when passing on news you heard from someone else.

phrases.en: We are expecting a baby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가까운 사이에서 부드럽게 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer expression used among people who are close.

explain_en: The current state of being pregnant is expressed in the past form '임신했어요'. Among close people you can also say '아기가 생겼어요'. Hospitals and the news use '임신'.

examples.en: A submarine can travel under the sea.
In the movie, the submarine hid from the enemy.
I went inside a real submarine at the museum.
The new submarine went down into the deep sea too.
They say the space inside a submarine is narrow.
My child likes a toy shaped like a submarine.

explain: 물속으로 들어가 다니는 배예요. '잠수부'는 물속에서 일하는 사람이라 소리가 비슷해도 달라요. 물 위를 다니는 일반 배는 그냥 '배'나 '선박'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I got on a submarine at the museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠수함에 직접 들어가거나 탈 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pair used for riding or boarding a submarine.

phrases.en: I like submarine movies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠수함이 나오는 이야기의 종류를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names a kind of story where submarines appear.

phrases.en: Inside a submarine, it's narrow and stuffy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '안'을 붙여 잠수함 내부를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 안 refers to the inside of a submarine.

explain_en: A ship that travels underwater. '잠수부' sounds similar but is a person who works underwater. Ordinary ships on the water surface are just called '배' or '선박'.

examples.ko: 아버지가 생일 선물로 전자시계를 사 주셨어요.
examples.en: My father bought me a digital watch as a birthday present.

examples.ko: 이 전자시계는 알람도 맞출 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can set an alarm on this digital watch too.
The digital watch stopped, so I changed the battery.
The date also shows on the digital watch screen.

examples.ko: 수영할 때 찰 전자시계를 알아보고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a digital watch to wear when I swim.
I set the time with the digital watch.

explain: 바늘이 있는 '아날로그 시계'와 달리 숫자로 시간을 보여 주는 시계를 말해요. '디지털시계'라고도 하는데, 전자시계는 건전지나 알람 같은 기능 이야기와 같이 나오는 일이 많아요.

phrases.en: There is a digital clock on the desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전자시계'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means almost the same as '전자시계'.

phrases.en: I'm wearing a digital watch on my wrist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손목시계는 '차다'라는 동사를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For a wristwatch, use the verb '차다'.

phrases.en: I changed the battery of my digital watch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시계가 멈췄을 때 건전지를 바꾼다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you replace the battery of a watch that stopped.

explain_en: It is the clock that shows time in numbers, as opposed to an analog clock with hands. People also say '디지털시계', and '전자시계' often comes up when talking about batteries or alarm features.

examples.en: The cursor keeps blinking on the screen.
Move the cursor behind the letter with the mouse.
I clicked where the cursor was and fixed the text.

examples.ko: 마우스 커서도 크기를 바꿀 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can change the size of the mouse cursor too.

examples.ko: 아이콘 위에 커서만 올려도 설명이 나타나요.
examples.en: A description appears if you just put the cursor over the icon.

examples.ko: 커서는 글을 쓰는 위치를 알려 줘요.
examples.en: The cursor shows where you are typing.

explain: 컴퓨터 화면에서 깜빡이거나 움직이는 표시예요. '크다'의 '커서'와 소리가 같아서 헷갈릴 수 있어요. '키가 커서'는 크다이고, '커서가 깜빡여요'는 이 단어예요.

phrases.en: The mouse cursor disappeared from the screen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마우스로 움직이는 화살표 표시를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the arrow moved by a mouse.

phrases.en: You can move the cursor with the keyboard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글을 쓰거나 고칠 때 위치를 바꾸는 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The action of changing position while typing or editing.

phrases.en: Write where the cursor is blinking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글을 쓸 수 있는 자리에서 표시가 깜빡이는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the cursor blinking at the spot where you can type.

explain_en: The blinking or moving mark on a computer screen. It sounds the same as the '크다' form '커서', so it can be confusing. '키가 커서' is 크다, and '커서가 깜빡여요' is this word.

examples.en: I like detective novels.
The detective found the culprit of the case.
My childhood dream was to be a detective.

examples.ko: 만화 속 탐정은 늘 작은 단서를 놓치지 않아요.
examples.en: The detective in the comic never misses a small clue.
The kids are playing detective.

examples.ko: 탐정에게 잃어버린 반려견을 찾아 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I asked a detective to find my lost dog.

explain: 탐정은 사건이나 사람을 조사하는 직업이에요. 경찰에서 일하는 사람은 '형사'라고 불러서 달라요. 한국 이야기에서는 소설이나 만화 속 인물로 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I watched a detective movie with my friend on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '탐정'을 다른 명사 앞에 붙여 이야기의 종류를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 탐정 before another noun to name a type of story or show.

phrases.example: 어릴 때 꿈은 탐정이 되는 거였어요.
phrases.en: When I was little, my dream was to become a detective.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업이나 꿈을 말할 때 '-이/가 되다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it with -이/가 되다 when talking about a job or a dream.

phrases.en: A smart master detective appears in that comic.
phrases.nuance_ko: '탐정'보다 뛰어난 탐정을 가리키고, 이야기 속 인물에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means an excellent detective, and is often used for story characters.

explain_en: 탐정 is someone who investigates cases or people for a living. A detective working for the police is called '형사', which is different. In Korean, the word shows up most often in novels and comics.

examples.en: Earth is a planet that goes around the sun.
Jupiter is the biggest planet.

examples.ko: 다른 행성에도 사람이 살 수 있을까요?
examples.en: Could people live on other planets too?

examples.ko: 이 망원경으로 행성을 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see planets with this telescope.
I memorized the names of the planets in order.

examples.ko: 영화 속 외계인은 작은 행성에서 왔어요.
examples.en: The alien in the movie came from a small planet.

explain: '별'과 구분해요. 태양처럼 스스로 빛나는 것은 '항성'이고, 지구, 화성, 목성은 '행성'이에요. 일상에서는 별을 모두 '별'이라고 부르기도 해요.

phrases.example: 다른 행성에도 사람이 살 수 있을까요?
phrases.en: Could people live on other planets too?
phrases.nuance_ko: 지구가 아닌 다른 행성을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to talk about planets other than Earth.

phrases.en: You can see planets in the night sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: '볼 수 있다'와 함께 하늘을 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '볼 수 있다' when looking at the sky.

phrases.example: 과학자들은 지구 같은 행성을 찾고 있어요.
phrases.en: Scientists are looking for a planet like Earth.
phrases.nuance_ko: '같은'을 붙여 비슷한 행성을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '같은' describes a similar planet.

explain_en: Do not confuse it with '별'. A self-lit star like the sun is a '항성'; Earth, Mars, and Jupiter are '행성'. In daily speech people often call all of them '별'.
